transcript:
Header: 2026-04-27 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~54m | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Janelle (Redwood PM), Devin (Redwood Solutions), Liam (Aurora PM), Priya (Aurora Eng), Carlos (Aurora SA), Hannah (Aurora Security)

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. agenda today is marketplace listing + reference arch + quick sync on security and next steps. we'll keep this to 45-60. quick intros?
[00:12] Liam (Aurora): hi, liam here, partner pm for auroracloud, priya and carlos on the call to drive the integration. thanks for setting this up.
[00:22] Sofia: awesome, marcus do you want to quick-blitz what we typically require for marketplace listings?
[00:29] Marcus (Redwood SE): yeah, sure, so high level we need listing metadata (SKU name, description, pricing model), entitlements mapping (who gets access after purchase), a deployment artifact (container image or AMI), and a reference architecture doc that shows network flows, auth and any infra as code snippets. also we recommend a starter repo for customers. apologies if i sound like a checklist robot.
[01:05] Priya: couple Qs off the bat — our team uses a private deployment pattern for regulated customers, sometimes with an on-prem package. for marketplace listing, do you have a separate SKU for private vs hosted?
[01:18] Janelle (Redwood PM): good Q. we typically do separate SKUs or entitlements. hosted api is one SKU, dedicated/reserved capacity another, and private (VPC/on-prem) is usually listed as a consult/enterprise SKU. you can map entitlements so that purchasing triggers a CSM kickoff for private installs.
[01:40] Carlos (Aurora SA): and the billing integration — does the marketplace handle metered billing or do we need to send usage back to the partner?
[01:48] Sofia: depends on marketplace. for Cloud marketplaces we support both marketplace metering and direct billing via entitlements. we can integrate with marketplace metering APIs or use a license key that unlocks the entitlement. for metering we'll need to map tokens/units to marketplace metrics.
[02:06] Hannah (Aurora Security): on security, we need to confirm SOC2 coverage, encryption at rest keys, KMS integration, and whether the control plane shares telemetry. can you clarify the private deployment model and what stays in the customer VPC?
[02:20] Marcus: sure. for private, the control plane can be either customer-managed or we can provide a lightweight control surface that only stores metadata. model weights and inference workloads run in customer VPC. for KMS you can bring your own key (BYOK) and we integrate with the customer's KMS endpoint. note: docs sometimes say KV cache as KV cash in the transcript; ignore typos.
[02:48] Priya: haha noted. for network flow, can you share a reference arch? we want to map to our hub-spoke VPC design.
[02:56] Devin (Redwood): we have a base reference arch doc we can share; it includes terraform snippets for creating peering, IAM roles, and helm charts for the on-prem operator. i'll attach the draft and a short deck after this. link: /shared/redwood/aurora/ref-arch-draft (placeholder)
[03:15] Liam: great. also curious about certification in the marketplace — is there a review process that takes long? we've seen 2-4 weeks sometimes.
[03:23] Sofia: yes, review can take 1-3 weeks depending on marketplace. cause for delay often are missing security docs or missing compliance attestations. so best to pre-seed SOC2 and SSO docs.
[03:35] Marcus: want to call out model variants and quantization. for marketplace listings we recommend publishing a recommended config for production (eg 16-bit quantized variant, batch size, KV caching enabled) with estimated egress/latency and cost numbers. we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet template.
[04:00] Carlos: can you talk through the expected latency profile for a default deployment vs quantized? our customers care about <150ms 95th for short prompts.
[04:10] Marcus: short answer: depends on model + hw. on A100 or equivalent, quantized 16-bit with batching and prefix caching typically can hit sub-150ms 95th for ~128-token responses. but it's workload dependent. we'll run a quick benchmark on the aurora test account to give you numbers.
[04:35] Priya: we'll need the benchmark harness and a sample dataset. do you have an automated script?
[04:41] Marcus: yes, we have a loadbench script that runs perf tests and outputs CSV. i'll push it to the repo.
[04:48] Sofia: let's talk deployment artifacts — does aurora prefer an OCI container or AMI?
[04:54] Liam: we usually prefer containers for marketplace images, but for some regions AMI distribution is simpler. can you support both?
[05:03] Janelle: we support both; container + helm chart is preferred for quick installs, and AMI + cloud-init for air-gapped on-prem customers. again those would be separate listing options.
[05:18] Hannah: about telemetry — what telemetry is sent to Redwood control plane? are logs or PII transmitted?
[05:25] Marcus: telemetry is primarily health metrics and anonymized usage — no PII. for private VPC deployments telemetry can be turned off; you can opt into local logs only. we'll document the exact telemetry fields in the security pack.
[05:40] Priya: SSO — we use SAML and OIDC. how's the SSO integration for the console?
[05:46] Sofia: we have SAML + OIDC integrations; for marketplace onboarding you can provide an identity mapping so we can automatically provision roles post-purchase. expect a small mapping script.
[05:56] Carlos: any blockers you've seen in prior marketplace integrations?
[06:01] Marcus: common blockers: missing SOC2 or audit docs, unclear entitlements, missing auto-deploy artifacts, and unclear support SLA language. also sometimes partners forget to provide a dedicated dev account for us to run final tests.
[06:18] Liam: queue — we will create a dev account and entitlement mapping doc and share.
[06:22] Sofia: perfect. next up let's sketch the ref-arch components and responsibilities. marcus, can you run through the diagram?
[06:30] Marcus: sure. top level: customer VPC hosts inference nodes (GPUs). optional ingress can be a private LB with mutual TLS to the customer's services. control plane can be hosted by Redwood or self-hosted in a managed container in the customer's cloud. KMS integration for key wrap; audit logs to the customer's logging endpoint (s3 or log storage). caching layer (KV cache) is optional and sits local to the inference pods. for on-prem we recommend operator-managed lifecycle via helm charts.
[07:05] Priya: any specific port or firewall rules customers need to open?
[07:10] Marcus: mostly outbound to S3 for weights if using shared weights, and to the control plane endpoint for optional management. if fully air-gapped we provide an offline bundle. we'll list specific ports in the doc.
[07:22] Hannah: regarding KMS, do you support customer-managed HSMs?
[07:26] Marcus: we support BYOK and some HSM integrations; we'll need the public endpoints/ca certs. performance-wise there is a minimal latency cost for every key unwrap. we'll note best practices for envelope encryption.
[07:40] Sofia: switching to marketplace metadata — items we need: listing title, short + long desc, logos/screenshots, entitlements mapping, pricing model, trial/consumption flags, support SLA language, docs link, and contact info.
[07:58] Liam: for pricing model, aurora would like usage metering via marketplace to avoid separate invoices. can redwood push metering events?
[08:07] Marcus: yes, we can. we emit metering events and can map token or inference-unit counts to marketplace metrics. we'll need the marketplace API creds to test in dev.
[08:18] Carlos: will the metering be per-token or per-request? some customers prefer per-request.
[08:24] Marcus: configurable. we recommend per-inference-unit (tokens*model-compute) for accuracy but marketplace constraints sometimes force a simple per-request metric. we'll document tradeoffs.
[08:39] Janelle: also thinking about listing verification — we can prefill much of the listing draft to speed review. sofia will share the draft template post-call.
[08:48] Sofia: yep will do.
[08:50] [09:00] Sofia: open floor, anything else?
[09:05] Priya: question about reference-arch CI — do you support terraform modules for customers to reuse?
[09:11] Devin: yes, we have terraform modules for peering, iam roles, and node groups. for marketplace we can provide a module that aurora can wrap.
[09:21] Carlos: regarding joint solution marketing, do you provide a co-branded listing or partner tile?
[09:27] Sofia: depends on marketplace, usually partner tile with co-brand assets. we'll coordinate marketing assets with your GTM team.
[09:35] Liam: security review — we'll need a SOC2 attestation and a quick security questionnaire filled. can you share a template?
[09:43] Hannah: and also need to know data residency controls for EU customers.
[09:47] Marcus: EU residency — we can pin model serving to eu-west regions and ensure weights and logs remain in-region. we'll note region pinning in the ref-arch.
[09:59] Priya: tiny nit — are there recommended quantization profiles per model family?
[10:05] Marcus: yes, we publish recommended quantization and kernel choices based on model family and sequence length. we'll share the recommend table in the ref-arch.
[10:14] Sofia: ok last section — operational runbook and support. what does a P0 look like and who escalates?
[10:21] Devin: in the listing we recommend an escalation matrix: CSM -> SE -> Eng on call. we can provide a canned runbook for failover, model fallback to smaller model variant, and how to flip to hosted fallback if capacity constrained.
[10:37] Carlos: fallback is important for us. how quick is the rollback?
[10:40] Marcus: automated fallback to hosted variant can be near-instant for routing level, but stateful KV cache warmup will take minutes; design assumes some cold-start cost.
[10:52] Liam: ok this is super helpful. can we recap next steps?
[10:56] Sofia: recap — we'll share: marketplace checklist + draft listing (Sofia), benchmark harness + CSV template (Marcus), reference-arch draft and terraform snippets (Devin), security pack including SOC2 sample (Marcus/Janelle). aurora will: provide dev/test account, entitlement mapping, and current onboarding terraform (Liam/Priya). schedule follow-up workshop wk of 5/11.
[11:24] Priya: thanks all, we'll get the dev account to you by 5/4.
[11:28] Sofia: great. I'll follow up with calendar invite and links. thanks everyone.
[11:33] [END]
notes: Shared artifacts referenced: /shared/redwood/aurora/ref-arch-draft (placeholder), /shared/redwood/aurora/marketplace-draft-deck (placeholder). Transcript contains minor transcription errors (KV cash, etc.) as typical in auto-exports.
